## Issues Found

### Critical (block merge)

### Major (revise before merge)
- `scripts/verify_plan.py:12165-12169`: c64 treats negated and future verification as completed full-grain verification.
  - Evidence: satisfaction requires only a full-grain phrase plus `verified|measured|confirmed|counted`; the deferred veto recognizes `will … assert`, but not `not verified`, `never measured`, or `will be verified`.
  - Impact: a sampled exactness premise followed by “not verified at full grain” or “will be verified over the full store” returns c64 PASS instead of WARN—the exact deferred-verification failure class this change is intended to catch.
  - Fix: reject negated and prospective completion vocabulary, then add fixtures for “not verified at full grain” and “will be verified at full grain”; both must WARN.
  - Mechanizable: yes — two pytest fixtures calling `check_exactness_grain` and asserting `status == "WARN"`.

### Bug-class sweep: unqualified completed-verification satisfiers
- `scripts/verify_plan.py:12107-12118` and `scripts/verify_plan.py:12165-12169` are the only `_C64_COMPLETED_RE`/deferred-veto definition and use in the file.
- No sibling implementation exists in another c64 path; registration at `scripts/verify_plan.py:12267` makes this one path load-bearing for every invocation.

- `scripts/verify_plan.py:12066-12076`: the exactness trigger is case-sensitive and misses ordinary casing of its own canonical vocabulary.
  - Evidence: `_C64_EXACTNESS_RE` has no `re.IGNORECASE`; it recognizes only literal `EVERY row`, while the newly added planner contract itself says `"every row"` at `.claude/agents/planner.md:582`. Sentence-initial `Every row`, `No exceptions`, `Exactly zero`, `All pairwise …`, and `Rows are byte-identical` likewise miss.
  - Impact: plans using the wording promoted by the workflow surfaces can receive c64 SKIP, so no mechanical warning is forwarded to the fact-checker.
  - Fix: make the exactness vocabulary case-insensitive, retaining noun scoping, and add parameterized casing tests for the canonical arms.
  - Mechanizable: yes — parameterize representative casing variants with a `706-row sample` marker and assert each WARNs.
